paper.title_en: Exploring the influence of microscopic nuclear densities and collective excitations on <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts></math>-induced fusion cross sections
paper.abstract_en:
Background: Heavy-ion fusion reactions offer a powerful means to investigate quantum tunneling in complex nuclear systems, especially in the near- and sub-barrier energy regions. In this regime, nuclear structure effects and the coupling between relative motion and intrinsic collective degrees of freedom play a crucial role in shaping barrier distributions and fusion cross sections. Accurate modeling of these effects requires reliable ion-ion interaction potentials and consistent treatment of collective excitations.
Purpose: The purpose of this work is to apply recently developed semiempirical and relativistic ion-ion interaction potentials to the description of available experimental fusion excitation functions for <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts></math>-induced reactions on a variety of vibrational and rotational target nuclei, within the coupled-channels approach.
Methods: The coupled-channels code ccfull is employed with newly implemented semiempirical potentials, for the first time, namely the São Paulo potential version 2 (SPP2) and the relativistic Brazilian nuclear potential (BNP), together with double-folding nucleus-nucleus potentials constructed from ground-state densities obtained within the relativistic mean-field and Dirac-Hartree-Bogoliubov approaches, folded with the M3Y and R3Y effective nucleon-nucleon interactions. Channel couplings are limited to the first low-lying collective excited state of the target nucleus, with deformation parameters taken from experimental data.
Results: The calculations show that the predicted fusion excitation functions depend sensitively on the treatment of pairing correlations embodied in the underlying nuclear densities, particularly in the sub-barrier energy region. While all interaction models considered are able to reproduce the general trends of the experimental data, differences emerge in the magnitude of sub-barrier fusion enhancement. The inclusion of pairing effects in the microscopic densities leads to a more stable description of fusion cross sections across light, medium, and heavy target systems. The observed enhancement patterns for vibrational and rotational nuclei are consistent with well established collective coupling effects.
Conclusions: The present study demonstrates that an accurate description of heavy-ion fusion reactions within the coupled-channels framework requires a consistent incorporation of pairing correlations through microscopic nuclear densities, along with realistic nucleon nucleon interactions and coupling to the first collective excited state. The recently developed SPP2 and BNP potentials provide useful reference benchmarks, while relativistic double folding potentials highlight the role of pairing in shaping sub-barrier fusion dynamics.
